quickSummary: VSEPR predicts 3D molecular geometries by minimizing valence electron pair repulsions (lp-lp > lp-bp > bp-bp). Steric number SN determines electron geometry, while lone pairs dictate the observed molecular shape.
summary: Master the complete VSEPR geometry spectrum from SN 2 to 7, including bond angles and non-ideal lone pair distortions.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 VSEPR Repulsion Principles & Steric Number
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 VSEPR Repulsion Principles & Steric Number

summaryBox.title: VSEPR Theory
summaryBox.takeaway: Repulsion: lp-lp > lp-bp > bp-bp. SN = bp + lp = 1/2 [V + M - C + A].

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
STERIC NUMBER (SN) FORMULA
                            
   SN = Number of Bond Pairs (bp) + Number of Lone Pairs (lp)
   
   SN = 1/2 [ V + M - C + A ]
   where V = central valence e⁻, M = monovalent atoms (H, F, Cl, Br, I),
   C = cationic charge, A = anionic charge.
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Repulsion Hierarchy**: Lone pairs occupy more spatial volume because they are attracted to only one nucleus, exerting intense repulsions on adjacent electron pairs:
$$\mathbf{\text{lp-lp} > \text{lp-bp} > \text{bp-bp}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Comprehensive VSEPR Shape Spectrum
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Comprehensive VSEPR Shape Spectrum
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **SN = 2 ($sp$)**: $2\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Linear** ($180^\circ$, $\text{BeCl}_2, \text{CO}_2$)
• **SN = 3 ($sp^2$)**:
  - $3\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Trigonal Planar** ($120^\circ$, $\text{BF}_3, \text{SO}_3$)
  - $2\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Bent / V-shaped** ($<120^\circ$, $\text{SO}_2, \text{O}_3, \text{SnCl}_2$)
• **SN = 4 ($sp^3$)**:
  - $4\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Tetrahedral** ($109.5^\circ$, $\text{CH}_4, \text{CCl}_4$)
  - $3\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Trigonal Pyramidal** ($107^\circ$, $\text{NH}_3, \text{PCl}_3$)
  - $2\text{ bp} + 2\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Bent / Angular** ($104.5^\circ$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{OF}_2$)
• **SN = 5 ($sp^3d$)**:
  - $5\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Trigonal Bipyramidal** ($90^\circ, 120^\circ$, $\text{PCl}_5$)
  - $4\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Seesaw** ($\text{SF}_4$)
  - $3\text{ bp} + 2\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **T-Shaped** ($\text{ClF}_3$)
  - $2\text{ bp} + 3\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Linear** ($180^\circ$, $\text{XeF}_2, \text{I}_3^-$)
• **SN = 6 ($sp^3d^2$)**:
  - $6\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Octahedral** ($90^\circ, 180^\circ$, $\text{SF}_6$)
  - $5\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Square Pyramidal** ($\text{BrF}_5, \text{XeOF}_4$)
  - $4\text{ bp} + 2\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Square Planar** ($90^\circ$, $\text{XeF}_4, \text{ICl}_4^-$)
• **SN = 7 ($sp^3d^3$)**:
  - $7\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Pentagonal Bipyramidal** ($72^\circ, 90^\circ$, $\text{IF}_7$)
  - $6\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} \rightarrow$ **Distorted Octahedral** ($\text{XeF}_6$ gas phase)

quickRevision: XeF₄ (4 bp + 2 lp) is Square Planar.
SF₄ (4 bp + 1 lp) is Seesaw; ClF₃ (3 bp + 2 lp) is T-Shaped.
XeF₆ (6 bp + 1 lp) is Distorted Octahedral in gas phase.
